label: ToLiss Airbus MCDU
description: Screen and keypad mapping for the ToLiss Airbus add-on's MCDU, under the AirbusFBW/MCDU{cdu}... namespace. Live-verified 2026-08-28 against a running ToLiss A330: read a real INIT page and the F-PLN page, and confirmed the keypad end-to-end (typed T/E/S into the scratchpad via individual key commands, watched it accumulate; CLR removed one character per press, matching a real Airbus CDU's backspace-style clear). Genuinely different screen shape from the stock A330's MCDU (see mcdu-adapter.js's own top comment on the two connect paths) — this profile and default-fms.json don't share any code path, changing one can't affect the other.
_note_provenance: Screen content and keypad presses are live-confirmed as described above. The exact color-letter-to-hue mapping below is lower confidence -- 'g' (green, seen on a live PPOS readout) and 'w' (white, seen on labels/dashes/placeholders) match real Airbus MCDU convention exactly; 'a' (amber) and 'y' (yellow) are standard-convention guesses not yet seen live; 'b' is assumed to be Airbus's cyan-ish 'blue' (the shade used for e.g. active waypoints/database-sourced data on a real MCDU) but unconfirmed; 's' isn't really a color at all -- it's a small symbol font (see _note_on_box_placeholder/_note_on_bracket_placeholder/_note_on_page_nav_arrows), so colorMap.s only matters for whatever 's'-colored text turns up that *isn't* one of the specific characters SYMBOL_FONT_GLYPHS special-cases. None of this affects functionality, only which CSS color class a character gets.
_note_on_rows: 14 rows total, matching the stock profile's own row count 1:1 even though the real derivation is different: title + 6x(label+content) + scratchpad = 1 + 12 + 1 = 14. Each 'cont'/'scont' pair (and title/stitle) are two sources for the same physical row -- confirmed live these are mutually exclusive (a page shows one or the other, never both), modeled as large-font vs small-font per src/mcdu-adapter.js's _recomputeColoredRow(). No reverse/flash/underline support -- no dataref for any of those was found in the supplied name listing for this screen, so every character renders plain (this profile's own _gap, not a mcdu-adapter.js limitation).
_note_on_keypad: AirbusFBW/MCDU{cdu}Key* et al. are complete command names already (no per-CDU prefix composition needed, unlike the stock profile's sim/FMS-vs-sim/FMS2-style commandPrefixByCdu) -- every key here uses commandTemplate with a bare {cdu} substitution instead. commandPrefixByCdu below is a harmless unused placeholder, present only so mcdu-adapter.js's _resolveKeys() doesn't warn about a missing one (nothing actually reads it once every key has its own commandTemplate). No CLB/CRZ/DES/HOLD/EXEC/FIX/LEGS/DEP_ARR/CDU_POPUP/CDU_POPOUT -- the real Airbus MCDU doesn't have dedicated hardware keys for any of these (that's a Boeing CDU/stock-FMS-profile shape), and none of the equivalent-looking ToLiss command names exist in the supplied listing either, so they're omitted rather than guessed. The 4-way SlewUp/Down/Left/Right cluster (a real Airbus MCDU control, used for cursor movement in some data-entry fields) replaces the stock profile's simpler PREV/NEXT/UP/DOWN concept -- new SLEW_* logical key names, not reused from the stock profile's UP/DOWN.
_note_on_box_placeholder: A real Airbus MCDU's 'mandatory field, not yet entered' indicator (a row of small amber boxes -- e.g. an empty CO RTE or FROM/TO on INIT/A) comes through as literal repeated 'E' characters specifically in the 's' color, confirmed live 2026-08-29. This is genuinely contextual, not a universal 'E means box' rule: typing a real letter E elsewhere (confirmed via the scratchpad) shows a real E -- src/mcdu-adapter.js's _recomputeColoredRow() special-cases only the exact (character='E', colorLetter='s') combination, substituting a box glyph in amber regardless of what colorMap.s says for 's' text that isn't this pattern. See _note_on_page_nav_arrows for a second character this same table remaps, and its own history of first being mistaken for real text.
_note_on_page_nav_arrows: A third 's'-channel symbol-font finding, alongside _note_on_box_placeholder's 'E'=box and _note_on_bracket_placeholder's 'A'/'B'=bracket: '2'/'3' in the title row's top-right corner (e.g. DATA INDEX showing '23') are left/right page-navigation arrow icons, not digits -- confirmed live 2026-08-30 by a user looking directly at the real cockpit texture and confirming they're genuine arrow icons, not text. This was originally misdiagnosed (2026-08-29) as a literal 'page 2 of 3' counter -- a plausible-looking coincidence, since DATA INDEX genuinely does paginate, so the digit interpretation happened to produce a sensible-looking number every time it was checked. Unlike the box/bracket placeholders (real 'mandatory field' warnings, amber and cyan respectively), these are plain page-turn chrome, so src/mcdu-adapter.js's SYMBOL_FONT_GLYPHS gives them their own white color rather than reusing either placeholder's.
_note_on_degree_symbol: ToLiss's screen text uses the classic Airbus/Boeing CDU font convention where a literal backtick byte (0x60) means the degree symbol, not an actual backtick -- confirmed live 2026-08-29 on the PROG page's BRG/DIST field (cont4w raw text was ' ---`  /----.-', i.e. '---°/----.-'). Unlike the box-glyph fix above, this remap isn't color-specific -- src/mcdu-adapter.js's decodeColoredChars() replaces every backtick with ° for all colors, since a literal backtick has no legitimate use on an MCDU screen.
_note_on_bracket_placeholder: A second 's'-channel symbol-font finding alongside _note_on_box_placeholder's 'E'=box: on the TAKEOFF PERF page, mandatory numeric fields not yet entered (V1/VR/FLAPS-THS/TRANS-ALT-style fields) render as a bracket placeholder, e.g. FLAPS/THS shows '[ ]/[ ]'. Confirmed live 2026-08-29 that the raw bytes are literal 'A' and 'B' in the 's' color (cont3s = '...A B A B'), i.e. 'A' is the left half of the bracket and 'B' is the right half. src/mcdu-adapter.js's SYMBOL_FONT_GLYPHS table maps both 'E'->box and 'A'/'B'->'['/']' for the 's' channel; the real letters A and B still render as themselves in every other color. Color: confirmed live 2026-08-30 this renders cyan on the real display, not amber -- amber was carried over from the box glyph's own confirmed amber on the unverified assumption both placeholders share one 'mandatory field' warning color; they don't. Matches colorMap.b (Airbus's cyan-ish 'blue'). The box glyph's own amber has not been independently re-checked against this same live-color scrutiny -- flag it too if it also turns out wrong.
_note_on_route_arrows: A fourth 's'-channel symbol-font finding, a second and unrelated left/right arrow pair alongside _note_on_page_nav_arrows' '2'/'3': confirmed live 2026-08-30 on an F-PLN page that '0' immediately before a waypoint name (e.g. cont2s='0...', cont2b=' RUNGA...' right after it) is a left arrow, and '1' immediately after one (e.g. cont3b='...ABEAM PTS', cont3s='...1' right after) is a right arrow -- both cyan, matching the adjacent waypoint name's own color, not white like the title's page-nav arrows. These read as inline route-editing markers (direct-to / abeam-point style), a different real concept from the title's page-turn arrows, which is presumably why ToLiss uses different characters for each rather than reusing 2/3. Same rows also show the confirmed 'A'/'B' bracket pattern (cont4s/cont5s = '...A B 1 ') alongside this new '1', all coexisting on one row. Wider-net caution applies more here than for E/A/B/2/3: 0 and 1 are common digits, so flag it if a real numeric 0 or 1 ever legitimately turns up in the 's' color somewhere. A third, separate arrow was confirmed the same session: '4' immediately before ERASE (cont6s='4 ', cont6a=' ERASE...') is a left arrow pointing at the ERASE prompt's own LSK, colored amber to match ERASE itself -- initially just an unexplained sighting with no adjacent text noticed, confirmed once a user reported '4ERASE' rendering instead of an amber left arrow. No matching right-arrow character found yet for the equivalent INSERT* prompt on the same row -- it uses a literal '*', not an arrow, so there may not be one to find.
_note_on_vert_slew_keys: The small up/down scroll-availability arrows in the screen's bottom-right corner (e.g. on a F-PLN page with more waypoints than fit on screen) are not part of the row/color grid at all -- a user found AirbusFBW/MCDU{cdu}VertSlewKeys, a separate plain int dataref, after the arrows were reported missing from the web panel despite being visible in the real cockpit. Confirmed live 2026-08-30 against a real F-PLN page with scrollable content: 0 = neither arrow, 1 = both up+down, 3 = down only. 2 (up only) is inferred by elimination (0/1/3 were all directly observed, 2 was not) -- flag if it turns out to mean something else. First implementation stamped this directly into the last two columns of the last content row (row `rows.length - 2`) -- wrong, confirmed live 2026-08-30 when a real 'INSERT*' message on that same row (F-PLN, pending revision to confirm) came through as 'INSER' with its last two characters overwritten by the arrows instead. src/mcdu-adapter.js's onVertSlewChange callback reports this separately now (see McduScreenView's own floating .mcdu-vert-slew overlay in mcdu-screen.js/css/mcdu.css), never touching the character grid at all.

keypadLayout._note: Same physical bezel shape as default-fms.json's own layout (a real Airbus MCDU keypad looks the same regardless of which aircraft simulates it) except utilityBlock, which uses ToLiss's real 4-way SlewUp/Down/Left/Right cluster instead of the stock profile's simpler PREV/NEXT/UP/DOWN.
